content:
The test image shows a soybean plant from ground level. Key observations:
- Green stems and developing pods
- Brown/necrotic dead leaves visible in the upper-left area
- Some yellowing on a lower leaf
- Stems appear green while leaves are dying off

This pattern (leaves dying/browning while stems remain green) is consistent with several diseases. Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome (SDS - leaves die while stems stay green), Phytophthora, or possibly Green_stem_disorder.

Let me view one reference image for Sudden_death_syndrome.

The SDS reference shows classic interveinal necrosis - green veins with yellow/brown tissue between them.

Comparing to the test image:
- Test image: whole-plant ground view, green stems and pods, dead/brown leaves in the upper area, some yellowing on a lower leaf
- The dead leaves in the test image appear uniformly brown/dried rather than showing the distinct interveinal chlorosis of classic SDS
- However, at advanced stages SDS leaves do die completely and drop (the brown crinkled dead leaves pattern matches late-stage SDS)
- Green stems while leaves are dying is a hallmark of SDS
- Pod set is visible which matches the R3-R6 timing when SDS typically manifests

The combination of green stems, developing pods, and dying/dead leaves at this growth stage is most consistent with Sudden_death_syndrome. The image angle makes it hard to see individual leaf symptoms clearly, but the overall plant presentation fits SDS better than alternatives.
